chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: When his playing was at its best
summary: He says he plays better every time in Denmark, yet Luis Russell's band was best.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: How about, tell me something in the many, many years that you've been playing the trombone you do feel you've gotten better playing? Has your playing improved since 1929?
When do you think your playing was at its best?
The Best? It was when I was in Denmark.
The last time I was there, and the time before that, and the time before that. Then every time I go, it's better. (Not bragging.)
It was better than the time that you were playing with Louis Russell?
Oh, that was the best of your playing you feel?
That was the best band I played with.
No, not the band but your playing. How you feel about this playing?
You played better with Louis Russell?

Yes. I played just as good with them I think. When you're playing with musicians and they all are not perfect but good musicians and they know what you're going to play and they know what to play behind you and ... what you going to play in front, this key (... their song .) ( ? ).
